But living semantic systems (evolving languages, scientific discourse in paradigm-shift phases) are *far* from equilibrium. If semantic coherence can be maintained — or *improved* — during phases where the token distribution is actively *moving away* from Zipf equilibrium, then the equilibrium framing is wrong. Kuhnian paradigm shifts are candidate cases: pre-revolutionary scientific language shows disrupted Zipf statistics yet *gains* semantic power during the disruption. Huffman coding on random strings produces near-Zipfian output distributions. If the Zipf signature is substrate-independent, it cannot serve as evidence for *semantic* thermodynamics specifically. F4 — The temperature inversion test**: INV_042 presumably links semantic temperature T to something measurable (e.g., variance in token rank-frequency slope). If a semantic field can be driven to *lower* temperature while *increasing* meaning — i.e., if semantic cooling produces richer, not poorer, expression — the free-energy gradient direction assumed by INV_042 is wrong.
